newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE holds 1997 gold forecast of US$375/oz.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE holds 1997 gold forecast of US$375/oz.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday it expected an average 1997 gold price of US$375 an ounce, unchanged from its February forecast and about US$25 above the current price.
The government forecasting agency also left unchanged its expectation that Australia will produce a record of about 302 tonnes of gold in 1996/97 (July/June), rising to 320 tonnes in 1997/98.

After falling to a three-year low of US$337 an ounce in February in the wake of central bank sales and disinvestment of gold from the private sector, the precious metal is poised for a recovery, ABARE said in its latest commodity forecast report.
Spot gold was fixed Monday afternoon in London at US$351.40.
ABARE said the role of large investors in gold would direct the market.

"While (gold) fabrication demand is expected to remain substantially higher than mine supply in 1997 and 1998, official and private investment sector demand will continue to be important determinants of gold prices in the short-term," ABARE said.

Demand from the fabrication sector is forecast to increase by over three percent in 1997 and 1998, mainly in response to forecast higher individual incomes in a number of key gold consuming countries, ABARE said.
ABARE said it expected reduced European central bank gold sales and tightening in the scrap market to result in reduced flows of above-ground gold onto the market this year.
"This reduction in supply, combined with strong growth in fabrication demand later this year, underpins the forecast recovery in prices in the latter half of 1997 and into 1998," ABARE said.
Growth in Australian gold production has not been noticeably affected by the recent decline in gold prices, ABARE said.
However, forward selling was providing a price buffer for producers in the short term, it added.
It is estimated that about 30 percent of Australia's 1996/97 gold production had been sold forward at an average price of about A$638 an ounce.
"This compares favourably with a forecast A$479 average spot price in 1996/97," ABARE said.
For 1997/98, it is estimated that around 50 percent of Australia's production is sold forward at an average A$610 an ounce, ABARE said.
